result:
I've committed the preparation and written `PREPARATION.md`. `./check.sh` prints CHECK PASSED (354 tests pass, all 906 report files match the baseline), and `./accept.sh` still reports the acceptance test FAILING, as it must.

**What changed:** everything that names or matches per-extension entries now goes through four small helpers in `SourceCodeAspectUtils`, placed just above `getAspectsPerExtensions`:

- **`perExtensionName(extension)`**: the name each entry gets. It still returns `"  *.java"`.
- **`decoratedExtensionLabel(extension)`**: the `"  *.java"` label. The indented lines of the text summary use it.
- **`extensionName(name)`**: strips the decoration back to the bare extension. `AnalysisUtils` now uses it to build the metric ids instead of its own `.replace("*.", "")`; the ids come out the same.
- **`landscapeAggregationKey(name)`**: the key the landscape merges entries under. It still just lower-cases the name.

Both landscape merge points in `LandscapeAnalysisResults` now call `landscapeAggregationKey`: the main/test aggregation and `merge(..)`, which builds the "other" category.

**Why it's cheaper later:** the task's own words (`linesOfCodePerExtension`, `"  *.java"`, `LINES_OF_CODE_MAIN_EXT_JAVA`, merge, "other" category) are now in comments at the spot to change. The code change becomes two one-line edits in one file: make `perExtensionName` return the bare extension, and make `landscapeAggregationKey` return `extensionName(name)`. After that, only the two existing tests listed in the task need updating.

**One small difference from before:** `merge(..)` used to match names exactly; it now lower-cases them like the main aggregation. The output can only differ if one repository had the same extension in mixed case, and real analysis output is always lower-case. The baseline comparison found no differences.
